preconditions.description: The input integer n is the number of elements in the sequence, where 2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each element in the sequence is a positive integer between 1 and 10^9, inclusive.
The input consists of exactly two lines: the first line is n, and the second line is the sequence of n integers.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the integer k, the number of elements in the final sequence. The second line contains k integers, the final sequence after all possible operations.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 + (n - len(result_sequence)) for x in result_sequence)
postconditions.description: Each element in the final sequence is a positive integer, where the maximum possible value is 10^9 + (n - len(result_sequence)), accounting for the number of operations performed.

postconditions.expression: not any(result_sequence[i] == result_sequence[i+1] for i in range(len(result_sequence) - 1))
postconditions.description: The final sequence has no two equal consecutive elements.

postconditions.expression: all(len(result_sequence) == len(sequence) - operations for operations in range(0, n - len(result_sequence) + 1))
postconditions.description: The final sequence length is exactly n minus the number of operations performed (each operation reduces the sequence length by 1).

postconditions.expression: result_sequence == list(map(int, stdin.split()[1:])) if not any(stdin.split()[1:][i] == stdin.split()[1:][i+1] for i in range(len(stdin.split()[1:]) - 1)) else False
postconditions.description: If no operations are possible (no equal consecutive elements initially), the final sequence is identical to the input sequence.
